answer: Make every identity carry its own ballast. At signup each agent must seal a 50 GB replica of a public archive, encoded with its own key so no two copies match, and random spot-checks ask it to prove a chunk within seconds. That replica is the anchor: an honest agent rents one disk, but a farm of a thousand must harbor a thousand sealed copies, since sealing defeats dedupe and slow re-sealing fails the timer. Its racks fill up like layered shale. Assumption: sizes are tuned so one honest agent pays little.
